title: No, I'm Not Selling You My Netflix Stock Today
author: Rick Munarriz
description: Netflix stock fell to a two-year low after Q3 earnings beat expectations but guidance disappointed. Revenue grew 11.8% to $12.87B and earnings rose 44% to $0.87/share, but Q4 guidance projects only 11.5% revenue growth and 15% earnings growth—the weakest performance in over three years. Despite six consecutive quarters of decelerating growth and key executive departures, the author maintains his long-term position, citing Netflix's historical resilience and current valuation at 17x forward earnings.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Stock hit two-year low with disappointing forward guidance showing decelerating growth (11.5% Q4 revenue growth, lowest in 3+ years), fourth consecutive quarter of slowing growth, and earnings growth expected to slow to 15%. Key executives departed and ad revenue forecast was cut by $300M. However, the author maintains a positive long-term outlook despite near-term challenges.

title: Netflix: 3 Key Takeaways for Long-Term Investors
author: The Motley Fool Team
description: Netflix reaffirmed its core investment priorities during its Q3 2026 earnings call, focusing 95% of capital spending on original content while advancing advertising technology and expanding global partnerships. The company's advertising tier is growing over 80% annually, and management prioritizes long-term strategic advantages over short-term revenue gains. Netflix aims to sustain double-digit revenue growth, expand margins, and increase free cash flow through superior monetization and global distribution.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Netflix demonstrates strong strategic positioning with 95% capital allocation to high-return core content, advertising tier growing over 80%, and management's commitment to long-term competitive advantages. The company maintains pricing power, expands global reach through partnerships, and shows confidence in its structural advantages despite short-term ad revenue adjustments. Financial objectives include sustained double-digit revenue growth and margin expansion.

title: Did SpaceX Just Save the AI Trade?
author: Neil Rozenbaum
description: SpaceX's Q3 2026 earnings report had a significant ripple effect on AI cloud stocks. The company's strong performance and its implications for AI infrastructure demand influenced sentiment across related AI companies including Nebius, CoreWeave, Nvidia, and Iren. The article examines what SpaceX's results mean for the broader AI investment landscape.

title: Netflix Q3 Earnings Beat Estimates, Ad Revenue View Trimmed
author: Na
description: Netflix reported Q3 2026 EPS of 87 cents, up 49% YoY and beating consensus by 6.1%, with operating margin expanding to 34.6%. However, the company trimmed its 2026 ad revenue outlook to $2.7B and free cash flow forecast to $12B due to slower-than-expected ad product rollout. Subscription revenue growth and strong performance in India offset advertising headwinds.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Strong Q3 profitability metrics (49% EPS growth, margin expansion to 34.6%) and record share buybacks ($4.8B) are positive. However, the company cut 2026 ad revenue guidance by $300M and reduced free cash flow forecast, citing slower ad product rollout. Management also acknowledged investor concerns about view hour growth. The Zacks Rank #4 (Sell) rating reflects these headwinds despite near-term earnings strength.
